Rankings layout (irw_rank family, data/rankings/README.md).

Description: Online survey experiment on ballot-order effects in ranked-choice voting, Alaska, October-November 2022: 354 respondents each ranked the four real candidates in the 2022 U.S. House race (task 1: up to four; task 2: all four, order reshuffled) and the four in the U.S. Senate race (tasks 3 and 4 likewise). One row per respondent x task x ranked candidate; item = candidate code c01..c08 in alphabetical order of the names (not stored), resp = position; trial_display_order = the randomised order shown to that respondent (codes joined by |), trial_contest, trial_required_full; covariates age, gender, race, party ID, education, likelihood of voting, state of residence. Rankings layout (irw_rank family, data/rankings/README.md).
Reference: Atsusaka, Y. (2024). Replication Data for: Analyzing Ballot Order Effects When Voters Rank Candidates [Data set]. Harvard Dataverse. https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/AJXRCV. Paper: Atsusaka, Y., Analyzing Ballot Order Effects When Voters Rank Candidates, Political Analysis.
Notes: Script data/rankings/atsusaka_2024_rcv_survey.py (file qualtrics_Alaska_nonnumeric.tab). Design record data/rankings/design_tables.csv. The deposit's Alaska cast vote records are FairVote files (alaska_2022 slice), not built here.

Description: Online survey experiment on ballot-order effects in ranked-choice voting, Oakland, October-November 2022: 259 respondents ranked the ten real candidates in the 2022 Oakland mayoral race (task 1: a ranking question with positions 1-3 observed; task 2: all ten, order reshuffled). One row per respondent x task x ranked candidate; item = candidate code c01..c10 in alphabetical order of the names (not stored), resp = position; trial_display_order = the randomised order shown (codes joined by |), trial_required_full; covariates (age, gender, race, party ID, education, likelihood of voting, city of residence) are Qualtrics numeric codes, since the deposit has no labelled Oakland export. Rankings layout (irw_rank family, data/rankings/README.md).
Reference: Atsusaka, Y. (2024). Replication Data for: Analyzing Ballot Order Effects When Voters Rank Candidates [Data set]. Harvard Dataverse. https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/AJXRCV. Paper: Atsusaka, Y., Analyzing Ballot Order Effects When Voters Rank Candidates, Political Analysis.
Notes: Script data/rankings/atsusaka_2024_rcv_survey.py (file qualtrics_Oakland.tab). Design record data/rankings/design_tables.csv. Task 1's question label in the export is a Qualtrics template placeholder; the items are the mayoral candidates.

Description: YouGov survey of 1,082 US adults (June 2023) built to study measurement error in ranking questions: 18 ranking tasks of 3 to 6 options each, every response a full permutation (anchor questions with meaningless 'Blank' items and one with a known correct order, substantive questions on government roles, identity, holidays, affective polarisation and electoral systems, two wording arms, and four repeated questions; randomised halves saw 8 of the 18). One row per respondent x task x option; item = option text (no option is a person), resp = position; trial_question = the question stem; covariates age band, gender, race, education, party ID. 12 estemporal responses with a repeated position dropped. Rankings layout (irw_rank family, data/rankings/README.md).
Reference: Atsusaka, Y., & Kim, S.-y. S. (2024). Replication Data for: Addressing Measurement Errors in Ranking Questions for the Social Sciences [Data set]. Harvard Dataverse. https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/UCTXEF. Paper: Political Analysis 33(4), 2025, 339-360.
Notes: Script data/rankings/atsusaka_2025_ranking_questions.py (ranking_error.zip -> ranking_error-main/data/raw/AmericanRanking_June_2023.sav; the archive's R code is GPL-3 and not used). Design record data/rankings/design_tables.csv.

Checked against the city's own 2009 cast vote record for this contest (identical ballots). The city counted by hand, on ballots rewritten by its Voter Error Accounting Chart: an overvote or a duplicate ranking ended the ballot at that ranking, one skipped ranking was closed up, and two skipped rankings in a row left a blank ballot. The recount rules are: one skipped ranking is passed over, a ballot that has skipped more than one (1) ranking ends there, and an overvote or a duplicate ranking ends the ballot (Code 167.60(a)(2) and 167.70(a)(2), where 2008-Or-028 and 2009-Or-102 agree on the skipped ranking; 2009-Or-102 was adopted on 2 October 2009 and signed by the mayor on 7 October 2009). A recount from this table with these rules reproduces every round of the city's tabulation sheet except for the difference below. The city defeated several candidates at once (batch elimination, Code 167.20 and 167.70(a)(1)c): a candidate whose votes plus every vote that could still reach them would not pass the next higher candidate is defeated with all candidates below. The batches are derived from the ordinance text, not from the city's order of defeats; the tabulation sheet names the candidates in each. In this STV contest, surplus fractions, transfer values and carried ballot weights are truncated to four decimals, as Code 167.20 says in 2009-Or-102 ('calculated to four (4) decimal places, ignoring any remainder', for the surplus fraction and for the transfer value). 2008-Or-028 has 'calculated to four (4) decimal places' for the surplus fraction only and no decimal rule for the transfer value. Difference (write-in merge, one ballot): the city's sheet counts one more first choice for the leading candidate and one fewer write-in than this table, and every later round follows from that ballot. The city's cast vote record (2009-BET-At-Large-CVR.xls) has one first choice typed as a write-in that names that candidate, and this table, like FairVote's file, keeps it as a write-in. With that one ballot counted for the candidate the recount gives every round of the sheet (2009-BET-Final-RCV.xls). The sheet applies the truncation of the amended text: it moves the leading candidate's surplus (6,032 of 16,728 votes) at 0.3605 of a vote per ballot, which is 0.36059... cut to four decimals, not rounded. A second counting program, written from the ordinance text without sight of the first program's code, gives the same tallies in every round except its last: it moves the votes of the last defeat or batch of defeats; the sheet's last column names it and moves no votes. The winners are the same.

The city counted by hand, on ballots rewritten by its Voter Error Accounting Chart: an overvote or a duplicate ranking ended the ballot at that ranking, one skipped ranking was closed up, and two skipped rankings in a row left a blank ballot. The recount rules are: one skipped ranking is passed over, a ballot that has skipped more than one (1) ranking ends there, and an overvote or a duplicate ranking ends the ballot (Code 167.60(a)(2) and 167.70(a)(2), where 2008-Or-028 and 2009-Or-102 agree on the skipped ranking; 2009-Or-102 was adopted on 2 October 2009 and signed by the mayor on 7 October 2009). A recount from this table with these rules reproduces every round of the city's tabulation sheet except for the difference below. The city defeated several candidates at once (batch elimination, Code 167.20 and 167.70(a)(1)c): a candidate whose votes plus every vote that could still reach them would not pass the next higher candidate is defeated with all candidates below. The batches are derived from the ordinance text, not from the city's order of defeats; the tabulation sheet names the candidates in each. In this STV contest, surplus fractions, transfer values and carried ballot weights are truncated to four decimals, as Code 167.20 says in 2009-Or-102 ('calculated to four (4) decimal places, ignoring any remainder', for the surplus fraction and for the transfer value). 2008-Or-028 has 'calculated to four (4) decimal places' for the surplus fraction only and no decimal rule for the transfer value. Difference (write-in merge, two ballots): in rounds 2 and 3 the recount has two ballots exhausted that the city's sheet counts for a candidate, and one ballot in rounds 4 and 5 (2009-MPRB-At-Large-Final-RCV.xls). Rounds are numbered as the recount counts them: the sheet has one more column, which moves no votes and repeats the totals of the column before it. The two ballots in the city's cast vote record (2009-MPRB-At-Large-CVR.xls) rank two different typed write-in names and then a candidate (c03 on one, c06 on the other). This table shows both write-in names as the same item, so the recount ends each ballot at the second one as a duplicate ranking. The sheet counts the ballot with c03 for c03 until c03 is defeated and the ballot with c06 for c06 to the end. With the second write-in name read as a different name the recount gives every round of the sheet. The sheet transfers no surplus, so this contest does not test the four-decimal truncation. A second counting program, written from the ordinance text without sight of the first program's code, gives the same tallies in every round except its last: it moves the votes of the last defeat; the sheet's last column names that defeat and moves no votes. Neither version transfers a surplus: c02 has 9,329 votes, 165 over the threshold of 9,164, before the last round. The winners are the same.
